name: Permit and Inspection Steps for Full Bathroom Remodels

step.name: Step 1: Complete layout planning and product procurement
step.text: Finalize your floor plan and order all fixtures, vanities, tile, and trim before demolition begins. Confirm lead times and check all physical dimensions against your rough plumbing openings. Done looks like having your materials on-site or confirmed for delivery, eliminating downtime while trades wait for parts.

step.name: Step 2: Demolition and structural inspection
step.text: Tear out old fixtures, tile, wall coverings, and subflooring down to the framing. Carefully inspect exposed studs and floor joists for plumbing leaks, dry rot, or historic framing issues. Done looks like clean, bare framing ready for mechanical rough-ins with any damaged wood repaired or replaced.

step.name: Step 3: Rough-in plumbing and electrical systems
step.text: Have licensed trades run new water lines, drain-waste-vent piping, dedicated 20-amp GFCI circuits, and exhaust ducting. Any layout adjustments or fixture additions take place during this phase. Done looks like all supply lines, drain traps, vent stacks, and electrical boxes secured in place according to local codes.

step.name: Step 4: Permit inspections and substrate waterproofing
step.text: Call in municipal inspectors to review mechanical rough-ins prior to covering the wall cavities. Once passed, install cementitious backer units and apply continuous waterproof membranes across all shower pans and wet areas. Done looks like signed-off rough inspection cards and a flood-tested, watertight shower substrate.

step.name: Step 5: Tile, drywall, trim, and finish carpentry
step.text: Hang moisture-resistant drywall, apply tape and compound, and lay tile across floors, shower enclosures, and accents. Follow with finish carpentry, including doors, casing, and custom baseboards. Done looks like flat, grouted tile surfaces, smooth painted walls, and clean trim lines ready for fixtures.

step.name: Step 6: Fixture installation and final sign-off
step.text: Set the vanity, mount the toilet, connect faucets, install shower glass, and wire light fixtures. Test all plumbing connections under full pressure to verify watertight performance and clear airflow. Done looks like a fully operational, clean bathroom backed by final permit approvals. If you are planning a full bathroom overhaul, reach out to HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866 to review your scope and schedule.
